header: "Show more": I fetch the list 100 rows at a time. For pages to be consistent (no one repeated, no one skipped between page 1 and page 2) the query needs a TOTAL order. The model's own ORDER BY is kept first (usually seniority, which is already unique per person); the position of every selected column is then appended as a final tie-breaker (ORDER BY ..., 1, 2, ..., n), so two rows can only be tied when they are identical in every column. I NEVER rebuild the model's SQL from its parsed form, because that can change what it means: the parser is used only to LOOK at the query, and the tie-breaker is inserted into the original text just before its LIMIT / OFFSET (or at the end). Returns null when the shape of the query does not allow it (a CTE, a set operation, SELECT *, unparsable): the caller then runs the SQL exactly as written and does not offer "Show more".

symbols.name: maskKeepingLength
doc: Returns the SQL with the contents of '...' strings and "..." identifiers blanked out, SAME LENGTH, so that positions line up.

symbols.name: tailStart
doc: Finds where the trailing LIMIT / OFFSET / FETCH of the OUTER query starts (outside any parentheses), or the end.
